direct_answer: Yes. Eni discloses a decarbonization strategy/plan as part of its strategic plan (referenced as the location for ESRS E1-1 “Transition plan for climate change mitigation”) [Source 11] and describes its “decarbonization strategy aimed at achieving Carbon neutrality by 2050” as integral to company strategy and governance [Source 10]. Eni also defines its “Decarbonization Plan” as the element of its strategic plan that sets objectives, actions and resources for transitioning to a lower-carbon economy, including reducing GHG emissions “in order to limit global warming to 1.5°C and achieve climate neutrality” [Source 6]. However, Eni explicitly states that its decarbonization plan “differs from the definition of the CSRD transition plan (ESRS E1-1) because it is built on the equity boundary” [Source 6]. Based on the retrieved passages, Eni asserts an intention to limit warming to 1.5°C within its decarbonization plan definition [Source 6], but the specific ESRS-required explanation of how its GHG targets are compatible with a 1.5°C pathway (including methodology/framework, scenarios, and assurance details) is not provided in the retrieved excerpts [Source 6][Source 11]. Therefore, 1.5°C alignment cannot be confirmed from the provided evidence. No timeline for adopting a transition plan is applicable based on the retrieved passages because Eni indicates it has a decarbonization plan/strategy in place [Source 6][Source 10][Source 11].
compliance_rationale: Evidence indicates Eni has a decarbonization plan/strategy connected to ESRS E1-1 and to a 2050 carbon neutrality pathway, and it references limiting warming to 1.5°C in its definition of the plan [Source 6][Source 10][Source 11]. However, the retrieved passages do not include the ESRS E1-1.16(a)/E1-4 type disclosures needed to substantiate 1.5°C compatibility (e.g., methodology, scenarios for target-setting, science-based validation, external assurance), and Eni notes its plan differs from the ESRS E1-1 transition plan definition due to boundary differences [Source 6].
disclosure_gaps: The actual content of Eni’s ESRS E1-1 transition plan (key actions, decarbonization levers, resources, and implementation roadmap) is not included in the retrieved passages (only cross-references are shown) [Source 11].

An explicit ESRS E1-1.16(a) explanation of how Eni’s GHG emission reduction targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C (beyond a general statement) is not provided in the retrieved passages [Source 6].

ESRS E1-4 details on whether/how targets are science-based and compatible with 1.5°C, including the framework/methodology used, underlying climate/policy scenarios, and whether targets have been externally assured, are not present in the retrieved passages [Source 11].

Clarification of boundary alignment with ESRS E1-1 (CSRD boundary vs equity boundary) and implications for the transition plan’s scope/coverage is not fully disclosed beyond noting the difference [Source 6].
